Proof in the paper: RuCo-300 and RuCo-400 only present well-resolved characteristic diffractions of (1 0 0 0), (0 0 0 2), (1 0 0 1), and (1 1 0 0) crystal planes for hexagonal close-packed (hcp) metallic phase. When the reduction temperature is increased to 500°C, a weak (2 0 0 0) diffraction for the faced-centered cubic (fcc) metallic phase appears, in addition to those for the hcp phase. As for RuCo-600, only an fcc phase is formed. In all cases, no recognizable diffractions assigned to Ru species are detected, suggesting the formation of the bimetallic RuCo phase.
